title: Why have a Brazilian club called out Cristiano Ronaldo over a historic transfer dispute?
content:
Brazilian club Flamengo and Spanish second-tier side Almeria are involved in a bitter dispute over a historic transfer deal, which has ended up in the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) and embroiled Cristiano Ronaldo.

The clubs are at loggerheads over the deal which saw Brazilian winger Lazaro join Almeria from Flamengo in September 2022.

Ronaldo, the Al Nassr and Portugal forward, bought a 25 per cent stake in Almeria in February — joining an ownership group led by the Saudi Media Company, the operator of Al Nassr’s stadium Mrsool Park, via a subsidiary of the forward’s investment brand CR7 SA.

In a statement released on Thursday, Flamengo claimed they are owed over €1.8million in Spanish taxes by Almeria over the deal for Lazaro.

“The case is objective and unequivocal: there is an express contractual obligation assigning to the Spanish club the responsibility for the payment or reimbursement of taxes levied in Spain,” it read.

“Nevertheless, even after Flamengo was compelled to bear such amounts — totalling over €1.5m — and following a formal FIFA decision fully recognizing its right to reimbursement, Almeria chooses not to fulfill its obligation. The debt after 590 days of default exceeds €1.5m.”

Flamengo’s official statement began with the italicised standfirst: “In February, the athlete Cristiano Ronaldo acquired 25% of the Spanish club”.

Almeria responded to Flamengo’s statement on social media site X, saying: “Issuing a press release as if the verdict had already been handed down, while the case is still in arbitration… what confidence in themselves! Or is it a new April Fool’s joke?”

A source close to Almeria, speaking on the condition of anonymity, suggested that Flamengo were using Ronaldo’s name to drum up publicity and pressure CAS.

CAS confirmed to The Athletic that on October 15, Almeria filed a case with the court, seeking to set aside a decision issued by the FIFA Players’ Status Chamber on August 4 regarding Lazaro’s transfer. The case was heard virtually on March 23 and the CAS Panel are currently in deliberation.

In an official statement of their own, Almeria said: “UD Almeria does not comment on ongoing arbitration proceedings. Nevertheless, Flamengo’s statement omits relevant facts, including those related to the Spain-Brazil Double Taxation Agreement.

“The controversy is submitted to the competent Arbitral Tribunal, and the amounts claimed are not owed. Any public pressure is inappropriate.”

Lazaro now plays for Saudi club Al-Najma, having joined them from Almeria in September last year.

Ronaldo is currently the best-paid footballer on the planet, earning more than £175m a year at Al Nassr in the Saudi Pro League.
